question: Does the fixed RAR plus squared-coherence-gated RG survivor remain competitive when it must infer its own galaxy nuisance parameters from inner radii and predict untouched outer radii?

NFW.equation: baryons plus one spherical NFW halo per galaxy
NFW.halo_parameters: V200 and concentration fit on inner radii with weak priors
NFW.claim_boundary: Flexible halo comparator, not a cosmological dark-matter population model

rethink_policy.candidate_fails_primary: Do not tune the three bridge constants on SPARC. Diagnose residual structure, then change or reject the coherence/density mapping.
rethink_policy.candidate_passes_but_is_indistinguishabl: Treat the candidate only as a cluster-side extension of RAR; it has not earned a distinct galaxy prediction.
rethink_policy.candidate_beats_RAR: Require replication with independent galaxy data and a relativistic raw-lensing forward law before advancing the theory claim.

claim_boundary: The squared coherence gate was selected after inspecting an earlier linear-gate failure.
The density field is reconstructed from axisymmetric disk, Hernquist bulge, and exponential gas proxies.
Per-galaxy nuisance parameters are calibrated on inner radii of the same galaxy, so this is radial prediction rather than new-galaxy prediction.
RAR and simple MOND are prior-art benchmarks.
The NFW control has two additional halo parameters per galaxy and is not a full dark-matter population analysis.
No relativistic photon law or theory-neutral lensing likelihood is supplied by this test.
